_doc: Category-30 (Culinary Oils and Fats) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-cat30.mjs — HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Numbers come ONLY from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, selected per subcategory by explicit scope regex, strictest across jurisdictions, at FACE VALUE (no reconstitution — an oil is not reconstituted). Pb/Cd/tAs/iAs/tHg are directly regulated for edible oils (EU 2023/915, Codex named-vegetable-oils, GSO 193:2021, Thailand MOPH 414/2020, Singapore Food Regs 2026, India FSSAI 2016, Israel FCS 2016). Nickel has no sovereign oil ML but a real hydrogenation-catalyst pathway, so it is held under a reflex screen (control), not declared not-material. Aluminium/tin/total-chromium have no oil pathway (not-material); Cr-VI is the reflex-speciation control; methylmercury has no marine methylation pathway in a plant oil (not-material). The honey-Pb near-miss failure mode is structurally impossible here: every unregulated cell resolves to control/not-material with a disclosed rationale that the audit pass tests against the register each build, never to an occurrence percentile.

olive-oil.name: Olive oil (virgin, refined, pomace)
olive-oil.audit_scope: edible fats and oils|edible oils and fats|fats, oils|fats and oils|vegetable oil|named vegetable|named animal fat|olive oil|olive pomace|olive residue|cooking oil|coconut oil|avocado oil|sesame oil|sunflower oil|palm oil|groundnut oil|canola oil|rapeseed oil|fat spread

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury forms by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish; a pressed or extracted plant oil has no methylation pathway and no mercury source. No government sets a methylmercury limit for a culinary oil.

Ni.rationale: No sovereign maximum level exists for nickel in culinary oils or fats. Nickel can enter a fat as residual hydrogenation catalyst (Raney nickel) in any hardened or partially hydrogenated fraction; virgin and refined liquid oils are not hydrogenated. Because a real exposure pathway exists, the cell is held under a reflex screen rather than declared not-material (the pathway would rebut a not-material determination).
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on each lot; any hydrogenated or partially hydrogenated oil is monitored under ALARA against the tightest available food nickel context.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign maximum level exists for total chromium in edible oils. Chromium is not lipophilic and does not partition into a refined lipid matrix; the only food chromium MLs in the register are dairy (milk powder, liquid milk). Rebuttable and audited against the register each build.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS as a screen; reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any total-Cr exceedance.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel number for a food; it is the toxic species obtained by reflex speciation. Any lot whose total-chromium screen exceeds the reflex trigger is speciated, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: IC-ICP-MS Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) on any total-Cr exceedance.

Sn.rationale: Tin migrates into food only from tinplate cans; culinary oils are sold in glass, PET, or lined containers, not tinplate. No non-canned tin pathway exists for oils. A canned oil would fall under the canned-food tin ML and is out of this subcategory's scope.

Al.rationale: No sovereign aluminium ML exists for edible oils (the only government aluminium food ML in any jurisdiction is AU-NZ infant-formula Al 500). Aluminium does not partition into a refined lipid matrix and a plant oil has no aluminium uptake or migration pathway. Rebuttable and audited against the register each build.
